title: Seals mirror your body language
topic: Why grey seals copy human posture on beaches, and what it actually means
voice_script: A seal will copy your body language back at you. Marine biologists noticed it first on Norfolk's beaches. Lie down, and the seal lies down. Raise an arm, and a flipper comes up. It isn't friendliness. Seals read posture to work out whether you're a threat, and mirroring is how they test the answer. Get too close and the copying stops. Then they bolt for the water. The mimicry was never a game. It was a risk assessment.
